open_questions: Rotation period 5.199 d vs transit period 13.5 d (ratio 2.605) with no flat-bottom shape and small phase curve - chance 5.2 d variability detected in 2 sectors cannot be confirmed as harmonic; detect additional transits to confirm ephemeris stability.
dossier.public_summary: The 13.5-day, ~1550 ppm dip recurs with a flat bottom, no secondary eclipse or odd-even change, steady depth and planet-sized signal. The star's 5-day spot signal does not reproduce the transit shape or depth. Together this is best explained by a ~3 Earth-radius planet on a slightly off-centre path.

reasons.why: Strongly flat-bottomed transit favours planet over V-shaped background EB or grazing EB.
3.0 Rearth (rp/rstar 0.0403, undiluted depth 1624 ppm) is planet-sized well below stellar EB regime.
Odd-even depth difference 475 ppm (depths 1603/1129 ppm, diff_sigma 2) is not significant at <4 sigma, no positive binary at twice period.
No secondary eclipse above detection; secondary depth 184.7 ppm with snr 2.4 well below odd depths, no stellar companion signature.
Depth steady across sectors (1473 ppm sector 42, 1250 ppm sector 82) so not depth-changing blend or spot mimic; neighbours.plausible_within_1px 0.
Short duration 1.999 h vs central 3.487 h (ratio 0.57) matches high impact parameter b 0.8679 fit, consistent with planet density ratio -0.2569, not duration mismatch.
Very small out-of-eclipse swing 77 ppm (ratio 0.0497 to depth) and chi2 6.741 dof 9, no large binary phase signal.
Planet-like rank above median planet at 0.59 and similar signals all are planets, supporting planet interpretation despite rotation period hint.
